name: Register Shift Detection
description: Detects unexpected shifts in linguistic register — AI text sometimes inconsistently mixes formal and informal registers.
mechanism:
This method applies Register Shift Detection for digital forensics and AI-generated content detection:

1. **Feature Extraction**: The input is preprocessed and relevant features are extracted using domain-specific techniques aligned with register shift detection.

2. **Statistical Analysis**: Extracted features are compared against statistical models derived from authentic content databases. Deviations from expected distributions indicate potential manipulation or AI generation.

3. **Anomaly Scoring**: A normalized anomaly score (0–100) is computed based on the magnitude and consistency of detected deviations. Higher scores indicate greater likelihood of AI generation or manipulation.

4. **Cross-validation**: Results are cross-validated with complementary detection methods to reduce false positive rates and improve overall detection reliability.
parameters:
Analysis type: automated statistical
Score range: 0 (authentic) to 100 (AI-generated)
Minimum input size: varies by media type
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-85% accuracy depending on input quality and method combination.
source: Based on peer-reviewed research in digital forensics and AI content detection.
useCase: Used as part of multi-signal analysis pipeline to detect AI-generated content.
strengths:
• Research-backed methodology
• Fast computation time
• Complementary to other detection methods
• Works across different AI generators
limitations:
• Accuracy varies with input quality
• Best used in combination with other methods
• May require calibration for new AI models
